name: The Brass and the Bone
creator: Dr. Peculiara Nzinga-Holmqvist, independent philosopher and retired BCI ethics consultant
description: A slow, rigorous neural-feed audio program released fortnightly, The Brass and the Bone examines questions of personal identity, continuity of self, and moral status in a world where memory can be edited, bodies rebuilt, and consciousness partially offloaded to machines. Dr. Nzinga-Holmqvist interviews neuroscientists, augmentation surgeons, BCI refusers, and people who have undergone radical identity modifications, treating each conversation as a philosophical case study rather than spectacle. The show is famous for its silences — Nzinga-Holmqvist is known to let uncomfortable questions sit unanswered for up to ninety seconds before moving on.
medium: neural feed audio / premium transcript archive (physical print available by subscription)
cultural_impact: The show's 2203 episode 'What Persists After the Wipe,' featuring a woman who voluntarily had her episodic memory cleared following trauma, was cited in three separate corponation court cases involving the legal personhood of memory-modified individuals and is considered foundational to the emerging field of post-continuity ethics.
controversy: A 2211 episode invited a representative of the Unclocked BCI refuser collective alongside a HelixCorp neural architecture engineer; the engineer walked out and HelixCorp subsequently pressured the show's distribution platform to restrict the episode's availability, which only increased its circulation.
story_hooks: Dr. Nzinga-Holmqvist contacts a fixer through an intermediary: a guest she interviewed three years ago has disappeared, and the episode containing a confession embedded in their conversation may explain why.

A corporation offers to fully fund the show's next season in exchange for a single episode framing their new memory-management product in philosophical terms — and Nzinga-Holmqvist is genuinely considering it.

A listener who has been modifying their own consciousness using techniques described in the show contacts the production team, claiming the process has revealed something about their BCI that cannot be explained by current neuroscience.
